description: One DrugExposure record says whether a Participant was exposed to one drug concept at one visit. Create one record per participant, visit and drug concept from the source yes/no variable; a source variable that is not about medication use does not become a DrugExposure. Absent and unknown answers are kept as records (exposure_status ABSENT or UNKNOWN), not dropped.

The coded drug or drug class, from the Variables file. Required. BDC-HM main describes this slot as RxNorm (DrugExposureConceptEnum, pv_formula CURIE, source ontology rxnorm); production also writes ATC class codes (for example ATC:C09A) and a few VANDF, NDFRT and MeSH codes. Only RxNorm (RxCUI) values conform to HM main DrugExposureConceptEnum. ATC, MeSH, VANDF and NDFRT codes are production practice outside the enum; VANDF and NDFRT are not in the project prefix table and are tier 3 until the Curator registers them, so a concept whose only primary code is VANDF (Taking oral hypoglycemic agents) cannot pass the promotion gate as it stands. Production codes stay as variants and no RxCUI is invented: an RxCUI is added only when it is verified in RxNav. Prefix spelling: write RxCUI: (the spelling gold uses in every file and this guide uses), not RXCUI:; both denote RxNorm, and the project prefix table should record RxCUI: as accepted. See the questions about whether ATC and the other prefixes are permitted. A concept's first Variables row is its primary code; variant rows are codes production already emits. Production returns the code only when the source variable says yes (a case expression), so check how ABSENT records are written before relying on the code of an ABSENT record.
Example source variable description: ASPIRIN/ASPIRIN-CONTAINING MEDICINES|Hypertension lowering medication within past 2 weeks [Cohort Visit Derived Variables. Visit 1]

description: How the drug record was obtained. Required. Values are OMOP Drug Type concepts; HM main has no value for 'questionnaire'. Interview and questionnaire answers about medication use are PATIENT_SELF_REPORTED_MEDICATION. Choose the value from how the SOURCE variable was collected, not from the drug.
Example source variable description: Did you take any medication for high blood pressure in the past two weeks?|TAKING MEDS FOR HYPERTENSION

description: Participant told an interviewer or answered a questionnaire (current use, use in the last 2 weeks or 4 weeks, regular use). Production uses this for almost every drug variable in every cohort. OMOP:44787730.
Example source variable description: ASPIRIN: CURRENTLY USING REGULARLY|Hypertension lowering medication within past 2 weeks [Cohort Visit Derived Variables. Visit 1]|Are you now taking aspirin or a medicine containing aspirin on a regular basis? This does not include Tylenol nor Advil.

description: A staff member listed the medicines from the labels of containers the participant brought to the visit (a medication inventory). Fits inventory-coded variables such as the ARIC Medi-Span coded medication derivations and the CHS and MESA coded drug-class variables. PROPOSED: production writes PATIENT_SELF_REPORTED_MEDICATION for these (see questions).
Example source variable description: Statin use in the past 2 weeks based on 2004 medication codes [Cohort Visit Derived Variables. Visit 1]|ACE Inhibitors without diuretics

description: The drug comes from an entry on a medication list. OMOP:38000178. Not used by production for these concepts.

A prescription was written. Production uses it for the ARIC hospital-form variable about IV diuretics during hospitalization and one ARIC calcium channel blocker hospital variable; an in-hospital administration fits INPATIENT_ADMINISTRATION better, so treat those uses as questionable (see questions). OMOP:38000177.
Example source variable description: Section 6: Biochemical Analyses. IV diuretics during hospitalization? [Heart Failure Hospital Record Abstraction Form, HFA]

description: Participant leaves the hospital with the medication or a prescription for it. Fits ARIC heart-failure abstraction variables such as 'ACE inhibitors at hospital discharge?'; production writes PATIENT_SELF_REPORTED_MEDICATION for them (see questions). HM main gives this value no OMOP code.
Example source variable description: Section 6: Biochemical Analyses. ACE inhibitors at hospital discharge? [Heart Failure Hospital Record Abstraction Form, HFA]|Section 6: Biochemical Analyses. Diuretics at hospital discharge? [Heart Failure Hospital Record Abstraction Form, HFA]

description: The drug was given during a hospital stay (hospital record abstraction, for example IV vasodilators or IV diuretics during hospitalization). OMOP:38000180. Not used by production for these concepts.
Example source variable description: Section 6: Biochemical Analyses. HFA73c. IV vasodilators [Heart Failure Hospital Record Abstraction Form, HFA]|Section 6: Biochemical Analyses. IV diuretics during hospitalization? [Heart Failure Hospital Record Abstraction Form, HFA]

description: Whether the participant was exposed at this visit. Required. Take the value from the source variable's own answer and its recall window (current, last 2 weeks, last 4 weeks, regular use). Map yes/no to PRESENT/ABSENT, a former-use answer to HISTORICAL, and missing, refused or don't know to UNKNOWN.
Example source variable description: ASPIRIN: CURRENTLY USING REGULARLY|Diuretic Medication Status (Y/N)

description: Source says the participant takes the drug in the variable's recall window (not a bare ever-taken yes, see HISTORICAL) (1, 'Y'; CARDIA codes 2 = yes for some medication variables).
Example source variable description: Did you take any medication for high blood pressure in the past two weeks?|TAKING MEDS FOR HYPERTENSION

description: Source says the participant does not take the drug (0, 'N'). Check the coding per variable: CARDIA uses 1 = no and 2 = yes for some medication variables, while CHS, HCHS and MESA use 0 = no and 1 = yes.

Source says the participant took the drug before but is not taking it now. Production uses it where an FHS value 2 means previous use (for example the FHS ACE inhibitor and hypertension medication variables). EVER versus CURRENT: taking a drug is an episodic exposure, unlike a chronic Condition (Condition guide condition_status rule 3, where an ever-had yes with no still-have item reads as PRESENT). A 'have you ever taken medication ...' variable answered yes with no current-use item does not prove current use: PROPOSED reading is HISTORICAL, and PRESENT only when a paired variable or the variable's own recall window gives current use. Production maps such a yes to PRESENT (see questions).
Example source variable description: Have you ever taken medication for high blood sugar or diabetes?|HAVE YOU EVER TAKEN MEDICATION FOR HIGH BLOOD SUGAR OR DIABETES?

description: Source value is missing, not asked, refused or unknown (for example 9 in the MESA aspirin variables, 'M' in CARDIA).

Age of the participant, in whole DAYS (BDC-HM unit d), when the drug was started. Fill only when the source gives an age started or an age first treated; production multiplies years by 365. Typical variables: age started regular use, age started hypertension, cholesterol or diabetes medication, age first treated. Production fills it only when the use variable is yes. Never fill it with the age at the visit.
Example source variable description: ASPIRIN: AGE STARTED REGULAR USE|HYPERTENSION MEDS, AGE STARTED USE|CHOLESTEROL MEDS, AGE STARTED USE|DIABETES MEDS, AGE STARTED USE|DIABETES: AGE FIRST TREATED

description: Age of the participant, in whole DAYS, when the drug was stopped, if available; otherwise it equals age_at_exposure_start per BDC-HM. No production file for these concepts fills it. Use it for an 'age stopped taking' variable if a cohort has one; never infer it from a visit.

The visit or exam at which the drug use was reported (for example MESA CLASSIC EXAM 1, CHS YEAR 10, ARIC EXAM 7). Optional in BDC-HM, but production always fills it. Hospital-record variables (ARIC hospital and heart-failure abstraction forms) go to a hospital-form visit, not a study exam.
The Participant the record belongs to. Required in BDC-HM; production builds it from the participant identifier and the cohort name.

Route of administration. Optional; fill it only when the concept or the source fixes the route: oral steroids ORAL and inhaled steroids or adrenergics ENDOTRACHEOPULMONARY (production does both in COPDGene and MESA). Leave it empty for class concepts whose source variable gives no route.
By mouth. OMOP:4132161. Used by Taking oral corticosteroids.
Inhaled into the airway and lungs. OMOP:4186832. Used by Taking inhaled corticosteroids and Taking adrenergic bronchodilators.
Example source variable description: Inhaled corticosteroids|Combination inhaled corticosteroid and beta-agonist

description: Under the skin. OMOP:4142048. Valid on HM main and fits insulin injections, but no production file sets it for Taking insulin; PROPOSED only where a source states the route.
Amount dispensed or ordered, from a prescription or dispensing record. Leave empty: these cohort variables are yes/no or recall items with no dispensed amount.
Days of supply from a prescription or dispensing record. Leave empty for these concepts; never calculate it from other fields (BDC-HM comment).
Intended refills at prescription time. Leave empty; no source variable for these concepts carries it.

The verbatim written instruction for the drug. Leave empty unless the source stores the verbatim instruction. BDC-HM has no dose or frequency slot: CARDIA 'TAKE ASPIRIN 3 TIMES/WK' and aspirin dose are not carried today (see questions).
Business identifier of the record, if the source has one. Production does not fill it for these concepts.
